Do you want hands-on experience of how innovative products move from idea to market? Are you eager to work with smart metering solutions that combine intelligent meters, software, data analytics, and services? Are you looking for an internship in an international green tech organization where your development truly matters?

Here is what your role entails

As a Product Management Intern, you will gain hands-on experience shaping our diverse product portfolio within smart metering, which includes intelligent meters, advanced software solutions, data analytics, and services. Moreover, you will gain practical experience across both strategic and operational product management, working closely with various stakeholders, including Product Managers, Research & Development, Sales, and customers.

More specifically, you will be:

• Gathering and analyzing customer, market, and competitor insights

• Supporting product roadmaps, business cases, project plans, and documentation

• Helping define requirements for new meters, software solutions, and services

• Contributing to innovation and early-stage development projects

• Tracking progress across product initiatives and communicating key updates

In this role, you will develop a comprehensive understanding of product management processes covering areas like hardware software, data and services. Furthermore, you will contribute to projects with real business impact while working closely with stakeholders across both functions and countries. As this is an internship position, you will also have the opportunity to explore your own ideas and interests within the scope of your responsibilities.

Meet your future team

You will become part of our two Product Management teams in the Water department, consisting of 16 dedicated colleagues in total. Together, we work with solutions that combine intelligent meters, digital platforms, software, and services. In our work, we inspire each other through the sharing of diverse perspectives and ideas that make our projects stronger and more exciting. Both teams have an informal and open culture where creativity is encouraged, questioning the status quo is welcomed, and exploring new approaches is part of the job.

Did you know? Our team is characterized by diverse international backgrounds, with employees representing five different countries.

Less about us, more about you

We are looking for a proactive and motivated student who is curious about technology and innovation and eager to learn more about product management in practice. Furthermore, through interaction with customers, you can understand customer needs, and help turn those insights into impactful projects and solutions.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Are pursuing a degree within Engineering, Business, Innovation, IT, or a related field

• Have an interest in technology, products, and customer-centric innovation

• Possess strong analytical and communication skills

• Enjoy collaborating with stakeholders from different backgrounds and cultures

• Have an interest in how AI can be applied in everyday work

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, this is an internship position, and we value curiosity and a willingness to learn just as much as experience. If the role interests you and you are motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply.

We offer more than just an internship

At Kamstrup, your contribution as an intern is highly valued, and we cherish the good colleagueship. Therefore, you will experience an internship with a strong focus on your individual development through challenging tasks, career sparring, voluntary courses, as well as social events and a large network. We are proud, that our internship program has resulted in Studenterhus Aarhus granting us with the Mentor Award, the Internationalization Award, the Jury’s Special Award and the award for East Jutland’s Best Internship.

Besides the best program, we also offer:

• A gratuity which may be provided in recognition of your efforts if your place of study allows it as well as paid public transportation to and from work

• Multiple internship events and weekly internship lunches

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association, that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

The applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, but you can expect a response within six weeks. Any details about the internship will be individually agreed upon. However, the internship is expected to run from the beginning of February 2027 until the end of June 2027.

Do you love designing clean game architecture, building multiplayer systems that run smoothly, and helping a team of programmers make the right technical decisions? Great! Let’s talk.

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

We're building something unannounced, exciting, thoroughly goofy, and built to be played together online. We're now looking for a Lead Game Programmer to help building the underlying systems that make it all work, from the core architecture to the multiplayer tech that connects our players. You'll stay hands-on in the code and the Unity editor while helping the programming team make good technical decisions, stay aligned, and build systems that support creative experimentation. And just to be very clear: this is a technical leadership role, not a people-management position.

**Here’s What That Looks Like Day To Day

**

• In collaboration with game designers, artists, and other programmers, you’ll build new features and systems and continuously iterate on improvements. We all work in Unity with C#, with every team member hands-on in the editor

• You’ll set and communicate the project’s technical direction, turning creative goals and production needs into clear technical priorities

• You’ll help the programming team make architectural decisions, align around shared patterns, and navigate trade-offs between long-term code health and short-term needs

• You’ll review and improve technical solutions, share best practices, and support other programmers without becoming a gatekeeper or bottleneck

• You’ll proactively identify technical risks, messy systems, and missing foundations, and take responsibility for addressing them at the right time

• Overall, you’ll make sure the project is technically healthy and maintain the codebase in a way that makes it easy for others to build on

**This includes things like...

**

• Designing an architecture that allows for easy gameplay implementation and flexibility

• Implementing and maintaining online features such as matchmaking, invites and friends

• Profiling and improving network performance, bandwidth and latency, and making sure the game holds up on real-world connections

• Breaking down complex technical challenges, helping decide what to prioritise, and ensuring important decisions are understood by the people they affect

• Staying close to the actual game: writing production code, debugging difficult problems, and improving systems as the project evolves

**You’re a great match if

**

• You have at least ten years of professional game development experience across multiple shipped games and different stages of development, including significant technical ownership or leadership on a project

• You have experience setting technical direction and helping a programming team make and implement architectural decisions, with strong judgment in balancing flexibility, maintainability, performance and the needs of a creative production

• You're highly proficient in C# and have deep knowledge of the Unity engine and editor

• You've shipped at least one online multiplayer game, had real ownership of its networking/online systems, and have hands-on experience with a Unity multiplayer framework (e.g., Coherence)

• You communicate clearly and can explain technical decisions and trade-offs to programmers and non-programmers alike

**Nice to haves

**

• You have experience shipping iOS and macOS apps, including hands-on integration of Apple platform services such as GameKit and the Game Controller framework using Xcode and Swift

• Experience with backend services, dedicated servers or cloud hosting for online games

• Interest in multiplayer game design and social features

• Experience working with automated build pipelines such as Jenkins

• Experience building systemic or open-world games

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**

• You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward

• You’re motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness and creativity while actively contributing to sustaining that culture

• You believe games are made by teams, not rockstars and that great ideas can come from anyone

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them

• You love exploration and experimentation but don’t get too precious when the evidence tells you you’re wrong

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place to be

**Practicalities

**

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• For this role we also consider people located outside of Denmark and provide financial (and moral!) support with visa application and relocation.

• We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10-15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

• Our working language is English.

**We offer

**

• Silly but ambitious projects, and the chance to work on and impact great games that reach millions of players.

• A playful and ambitious work environment where experimentation is encouraged.

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games.

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth.

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, team events, you name it.

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant just a walk across the lakes away, with plant-based options (and soft ice on Thursdays).

• Six weeks of vacation (five standard plus one extra on us).

• Paid parental leave at full salary for the periods covered by state reimbursement.

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked.

• Pension plan and private health insurance.

• Endless amounts of Faxe Kondi.

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, which is played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make everyone laugh. To do so, we focus on exploring comedy through gameplay. We like to break player expectations, use wonderful music, slick art, and create a quirky atmosphere. We experiment a lot, and it doesn't always work out, but we always learn something.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games, and we believe diversity makes for better teams. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and will challenge us and our way of doing things.

jobs.occupation: A Post doc position is available in the Grønbæk Group at Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC),
jobs.description:
We are searching for a skilled and experienced post doc with specific interest in investigating early myeloid disease, clonal haematopoiesis, metabolism and obesity.

  Our research/The group

  The focus of the Grønbæk group is Translational Haematology. The group is affiliated with Biotech Research and Innovation centre (BRIC), University of Copenhagen and Rigshospitalet (Central Copenhagen University Hospital). 

  Our overall aim is to understand the molecular mechanisms of haematological cancers and based on this; to design, develop and implement novel, scientifically based, clinical trials, with a strong focus on epigenetic therapies. This is done by bridging between clinical research at Rigshospitalet and the basic cancer biology research at BRIC, and in international collaborations with, among others, the Van Andel Research Institute, Michigan, USA and the Nordic MDS study group.

  Our location at the Copenhagen Biocentre/BRIC provides optimal conditions for interaction with the basic scientists at BRIC. The group currently consists of 14 scientists, MD/scientists and students, one clinical research coordinator, 1 research nurse and 2 biomedical laboratory scientists.

   

  The project: Deciphering the Mechanistic Links Between Obesity, Clonal Haematopoiesis and Myeloid Neoplasms.

  The current position is part of a joint project ‘Deciphering the Mechanistic Links Between Obesity, Clonal Haematopoiesis and Myeloid Neoplasms’ together with Professor George Vassiliou, Cambridge Stem Cell Institute, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom funded by a ‘Molecular Mechanisms Linking Obesity and Cancer (MMLOC)’ grant from the Novo Nordisk foundation, which supports collaborative research projects with the purpose ‘to reverse-translate clinical observations into mechanistic studies that will increase our understanding of how obesity impacts carcinogenesis’.

  Obesity is a global health issue linked to increased risk of cancer, including blood cancers such as myeloid neoplasms (MN). Many MN arise from clonal haematopoiesis (CH)—the abnormal expansion of blood stem cell clones carrying somatic mutations. Haematopoietic stem cells interact with bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT), which increases with obesity, which may fuel CH growth and progression to MN. Epidemiological and genetic studies already suggest obesity accelerates CH, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

  This project integrates large-scale population data, clinical trials, and mechanistic mouse studies to investigate these links and explore preventive or therapeutic strategies.

   

  Your job

  The project focuses on translational analyses of live frozen human cells from patient bone marrow (BM)/(BMAT) and blood samples from completed and ongoing clinical trials. We are searching for a skilled post doc who is very interactive and enjoys collaborations with other scientists – including younger scientists and clinician scientists.

  Your tasks will include:

   	
• Process of live frozen patient material from clinical trials including isolation of defined cell populations, and quality control for downstream omics 	
• Perform in-house molecular techniques which may include Proteomics, PCR, ddPCR, and library/sample preparation for RNA-seq, ATAC-seq and DNA methylation analyses 	
• Coordinate genomic, transcriptomic, lipidomic, metabolomic analyses with our internal and external collaborating laboratories and take the lead on designing relevant sub-studies, integrating and interpreting the data 	
• Help establish the practical and regulatory framework for these collaborations, including material transfer and data-sharing agreements 	
• Participate in grant and manuscript writing 	
• Present at local and international meetings 	
• Introduce lab techniques to new lab members and students 	
• Collaborate with both scientists and clinicians   Start: February 1st, 2027

  Duration: 2 years

  Profile

  We expect you to be a highly motivated and highly ambitious, independent scientist with the following qualifications: •

   	
• A PhD in Life Sciences with a preferred focus on haematology 	
• A strong background in mechanisms of normal and malignant haematopoiesis and molecular haematology techniques 	
• Comprehensive lab skills in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including work with primary human cells and cryopreserved patient material 	
• Experience with genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, lipidomics, metabolomics and ability to analyse and interpret such data 	
• Experience with running projects across research groups 	
• Strong publication and presentation record in peer reviewed journals and international conferences 	
• Excellent written and spoken English skills 	
• Very collaborative 	
• Good social skills     

  Place of employment
 The workplace is at the Bartholin Institute which is part of Rigshospitalet, University of Copenhagen. The Bartholin Institute is located at Copenhagen Biocentre/BRIC, close to the centre of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and a number of core facilities (animal unit, flow cytometry, in vivo imaging, NGS, etc.) shared between the research groups at BRIC (www.bric.ku.dk) and the neighbouring Finsen Laboratory. We have weekly journal clubs, data clubs, seminars with invited speakers and a young researchers club ASAP and our own PhD programme, MoMeD.

   

  Terms of employment 
 The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of two years. The starting date is 01.02.2027 or after agreement.
 Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 39,900 DKK/approx. 5,300 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025

   

  Questions 

  For further information regarding the position, please contact Professor Kirsten Grønbæk, kirsten groenbaek@regionh.dk; phone + 4535456086 / +4525211598.

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

   

  Application
 The application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

  1. Motivated letter of application (max. one page).

  2. CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position.

  3. A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do.

  4. List of publications.

   

  Recommendation 
 Furthermore, the applicant should provide two letters of recommendation or two references. To be taken into consideration, the letters must be signed by the supporting person on paper with institutional letter head and in PDF-format.

   

  Application deadline 15 November 2026, 23.59pm CET.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications 3 of 4 or letters of recommendation that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

   

  The further process

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

You will ensure that requirements, design decisions, implementation, integration, testing, and validation remain connected throughout the development lifecycle. The role requires strong RF system understanding, structured systems-engineering expertise, technical ownership, and a hands-on integration mindset. Working with technical leadership, you will turn product and architectural intent into an executable, traceable, and verifiable engineering baseline and help carry the product through integration, qualification, and deployment.

Key responsibilities

• Translate product, mission, and stakeholder needs into clear functional, performance, parametric, interface, environmental, and verification requirements.

• Develop and maintain the functional and physical system architecture, allocate requirements to subsystems, and define key technical trade-offs.

• Establish and maintain system performance budgets and constraints covering RF performance, timing and synchronization, data flow, power, thermal performance, mass, and platform interfaces.

• Define and maintain system requirements, subsystem requirements, interface control documentation, acceptance criteria, and verification logic.

• Align RF subsystem requirements, including frequency coverage, sensitivity, selectivity, dynamic range, noise figure, linearity, phase noise, spurious responses, channel isolation, and interference resilience.

• Define antenna-system requirements covering frequency coverage, antenna gain, polarization, radiation-pattern characteristics, isolation between antenna channels, placement, and platform integration.

• Define embedded control, data acquisition, timing, synchronization, diagnostics, logging, networking, and system-monitoring requirements.

• Coordinate mechanical and platform requirements covering dimensions, mass, thermal management, connectors, cabling, grounding, shielding, mounting, environmental constraints, and serviceability.

• Work with RF test and characterization engineers to define measurable acceptance criteria, calibration needs, verification methods, test coverage, and required evidence.

• Prepare and maintain system requirements specifications, interface-control documents, system budgets, integration plans, verification plans, compliance matrices, and technical decision records.

• Lead system integration planning and support prototype bring-up, laboratory validation, qualification, and field-test preparation.

• Identify system-level risks, interface conflicts, missing requirements, invalid assumptions, and integration blockers, and drive their resolution.

• Facilitate cross-functional technical alignment between engineering disciplines, technical leadership, manufacturing partners, and partner engineering teams.

• Support requirements reviews, system design reviews, integration reviews, test readiness reviews, and milestone decisions.

• Maintain traceability between stakeholder needs, requirements, design decisions, implementation, verification results, and acceptance evidence.

• Help establish systems-engineering methods, documentation practices, requirements-management workflows, and technical-review processes for future MITS Industries development programs.

Required qualifications and experience

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in electrical or electronic engineering, telecommunications, systems engineering, aerospace engineering, applied physics, or a related field.

• 6+ years of professional experience in systems engineering for complex RF, electronic, aerospace, or other mission-critical systems.

• Strong understanding of RF systems, including receiver architectures, RF signal paths, antenna interfaces, signal acquisition, data conversion, embedded control, timing and synchronization, calibration, and system validation.

• Proven experience translating product, mission, and stakeholder needs into functional, performance, parametric, interface, environmental, and verification requirements.

• Experience developing functional and physical system architectures, decomposing systems into subsystems, allocating requirements, and defining interfaces and technical trade-offs.

• Experience establishing and maintaining system performance budgets and constraints covering RF performance, timing and synchronization, data flow, power, thermal performance, mass, and platform interfaces.

• Strong understanding of requirements decomposition, traceability, acceptance criteria, and verification methods, including analysis, inspection, demonstration, and testing.

• Experience preparing and maintaining system requirements specifications, interface-control documents, integration plans, verification plans, compliance matrices, and technical decision records.

• Practical experience with requirements-management and traceability tools such as IBM Engineering DOORS, Jama Connect, Polarion, or equivalent.

• Experience working with cross-functional engineering teams covering RF and microwave hardware, antennas, embedded systems, signal processing, mechanical design, test, manufacturing, and system integration.

• Ability to evaluate technical trade-offs across RF performance, embedded implementation, mechanical and thermal constraints, testability, manufacturability, reliability, and operational use.

• Hands-on experience with prototype integration, laboratory validation, system-level debugging, and troubleshooting of complex multidisciplinary systems.

• Experience identifying and managing system-level risks, interface conflicts, assumptions, technical dependencies, and integration blockers. Strong technical communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to align senior engineers and drive decisions across engineering disciplines.

Nice to have

• Experience with signal-intelligence, direction-finding, spectrum-monitoring, or radio-surveillance systems.

• Experience with SDR-based systems and high-throughput RF data acquisition.

• Experience with broadband, multiband, coherent, or multichannel receiver systems.

• Experience with Model-Based Systems Engineering, SysML, and tools such as Cameo Systems Modeler, Enterprise Architect, or equivalent.

• Experience establishing and maintaining controlled system baselines, including requirements, interfaces, verification status, configuration, and engineering changes.

• Experience with engineering analysis, data processing, or system modelling using MATLAB, Python, or equivalent.

• Experience with field integration, testing, calibration, and deployment of complex RF or aerospace systems.

• Experience working on aerospace, mission-critical, ruggedized, or internationally distributed engineering programs.

Success in the first 6 months

• Establish the initial system requirements baseline, subsystem allocation, interface definitions, and performance budgets for the assigned product scope.

• Create a clear technical decomposition across RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, embedded control, signal processing, mechanical design, test, and system integration.

• Define the integration, verification, and validation approach for the initial prototype or subsystem, including acceptance criteria, traceability, and required evidence.

• Identify unclear interfaces, missing requirements, technical assumptions, and system-level risks early, and drive practical resolution actions. Support prototype integration, bring-up, and laboratory validation with structured system-level analysis, troubleshooting, and verification evidence.

• Establish repeatable systems-engineering practices, documentation templates, requirements-management workflows, and technical-review processes for future development programs.

🇩🇰 ER DU VORES NYE MEDARBEJDER?

Tiltrædelse hurtigst muligt!

RenTid søger en erfaren rengøringsassistent til en fuldtidsstilling på 37 timer om ugen med mulighed for merarbejde.

Læs og forstå hele opslaget, før du ansøger. Vi forventer, at du har læst og forstået opslaget, inden du søger stillingen. Ansøgninger fra personer, der ikke opfylder de grundlæggende krav i opslaget, vil ikke komme i betragtning.

RenTid er en virksomhed i vækst, og vi søger en erfaren rengøringsassistent, som er dygtig til sit håndværk og har lyst til at udvikle sig sammen med os. Hos RenTid spiller øje for et perfekt resultat og sans for detaljen en stor rolle.

Du bliver ansat som rengøringsassistent og skal først og fremmest levere rengøring af høj kvalitet hos vores kunder i Aarhus og omegn.

Vi ser ikke kun på dit CV – vi ser på din arbejdsmoral, ansvarlighed, kvalitet og lyst til at udvikle dig.

🇩🇰 🚀 MULIGHED FOR UDVIKLING

Når RenTid vokser, opstår der nye muligheder. Den rette medarbejder kan med tiden få ansvar for eksempelvis:

• 
Kvalitetskontrol

• 
Oplæring af nye medarbejdere

• 
Kundekontakt

• 
Koordinering og planlægning

• 
Teamlederfunktioner

• 
Større driftsansvar

Hvor langt du kan komme, afhænger i høj grad af dig.

🇩🇰 🧹 VI FORVENTER, AT DU:

• 
Har solid erfaring med rengøring i private hjem.

• 
Ikke er bange for at arbejde alene.

• 
Gerne har erfaring med erhvervsrengøring.

• 
Arbejder selvstændigt og grundigt, men også kan fungere i mindre teams.

• 
Har øje for detaljer og kvalitet.

• 
Er mødestabil, fleksibel og ansvarsbevidst.

• 
Har en positiv indstilling og tager imod feedback.

• 
Har kørekort B og ikke er bange for at køre bil er et "Must". Du skal ikke søge stillingen, hvis du ikke har kørekort og lyst til at køre bil.

• 
Selv kan komme til og fra arbejdspladsen i Aarhus.

• 
Er indstillet på, at der kan forekomme weekendarbejde. Kan du ikke arbejde i weekenderne, så er RenTid ikke stedet for dig.

🇬🇧 SPROG – VIGTIGT

Du skal kunne tale, forstå, læse og skrive flydende engelsk.

Du skal ikke søge stillingen, hvis du ikke taler og forstår engelsk.

Dansk er en klar fordel, men ikke et krav.

⏱️ PRØVEPERIODE

De første 3 måneder er en prøveperiode efter gældende danske regler.

Her vurderer vi blandt andet din arbejdsindsats, kvalitet, samarbejde, ansvarlighed og udvikling.

💰 LØN OG MULIGHEDER

Du får en god og ordentlig løn fra starten.

Din startløn vil være 145,00 kr. pr. time, plus 12,5 % feriepenge og ATP efter gældende regler.

Større ansvar, højere løn og andre goder følger med, når du viser, at du kan løfte mere.

Efter de 3 måneders prøvetid har du mulighed for at genforhandle din løn ud fra de kvalifikationer og den udvikling, du har vist os i løbet af prøveperioden.

Vi leder efter en person, der ikke bare søger et job – men gerne vil være en del af RenTids udvikling.

📍 ARBEJDSOMRÅDE

Aarhus og omegn.

RenTid stiller bil til rådighed for dig eller teamet i arbejdstiden.

📩 LYDER DET SOM DIG?

Send os en motiveret ansøgning og CV med billede.

Fortæl kort om:

• 
Dig selv

• 
Din erfaring med rengøring

• 
Din erfaring med private hjem

• 
Eventuel erfaring med erhvervsrengøring

• 
Hvad du gerne vil udvikle dig inden for

Ansøgningen skal være på engelsk.

Vi indkalder løbende til samtaler.

🇬🇧 ARE YOU OUR NEW EMPLOYEE?

Start date: As soon as possible!

RenTid is looking for an experienced cleaning assistant for a full-time position of 37 hours per week, with the possibility of additional hours.

Please read and understand the entire job advertisement before applying. We expect you to have read and understood the advertisement before applying for the position. Applications from candidates who do not meet the basic requirements will not be considered.

RenTid is a growing company, and we are looking for an experienced cleaning assistant who is skilled at their workand motivated to develop and grow with us. At RenTid, attention to detail and delivering a perfect result are extremely important.

You will be employed as a cleaning assistant, and your primary responsibility will be to provide high-quality cleaningfor our customers in Aarhus and the surrounding area.

We do not only look at your CV – we look at your work ethic, responsibility, quality of work and willingness to develop.

🚀 OPPORTUNITIES FOR DEVELOPMENT

As RenTid grows, new opportunities will arise. The right employee may, over time, take on responsibility for areas such as:

• 
Quality control

• 
Training new employees

• 
Customer contact

• 
Coordination and planning

• 
Team leader responsibilities

• 
Greater operational responsibility

How far you can go depends largely on you.

🧹 WE EXPECT YOU TO:

• 
Have solid experience in residential cleaning.

• 
Not be afraid of working independently.

• 
Preferably have experience with commercial cleaning.

• 
Be able to work independently and thoroughly, while also being comfortable working in small teams.

• 
Have a strong eye for detail and quality.

• 
Be reliable, flexible and responsible.

• 
Have a positive attitude and be open to feedback.

• 
Have a valid Category B driving licence and be comfortable driving a car – this is a MUST. Please do not apply if you do not have a driving licence or are not willing to drive.

• 
Be able to get to and from the workplace in Aarhus independently.

• 
Be prepared for occasional weekend work. If you are unable to work weekends, RenTid is not the right place for you.

You must be able to speak, understand, read and write fluent English.

Please do not apply if you do not speak and understand English.

Danish is a clear advantage, but not a requirement.

The first 3 months will be a probationary period in accordance with applicable Danish rules.

During this period, we will evaluate your work performance, quality, cooperation, responsibility and development.

You will receive a fair and competitive salary from the beginning.

Your starting salary will be DKK 145.00 per hour, plus 12.5% holiday pay and ATP in accordance with applicable Danish rules.

Greater responsibility, higher pay and other benefits will follow as you demonstrate that you are capable of taking on more responsibility.

After the 3-month probationary period, you will have the opportunity to renegotiate your salary based on the qualifications and development you have demonstrated during the probationary period.

We are looking for someone who is not just looking for a job – but someone who wants to become part of RenTid’s continued development.

📍 WORK AREA

Aarhus and surrounding areas.

RenTid provides a company car for you or the team during working hours.

📩 DOES THIS SOUND LIKE YOU?

Send us a motivated application and CV with a photo.

Please briefly tell us about:

• 
Yourself

• 
Your experience in cleaning

• 
Your experience with residential cleaning

• 
Any experience with commercial cleaning

• 
What areas you would like to develop your skills in

Your application must be written in English.

We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis.

FirePoint Rocket Technology is building one of the most unique and strategically important industrial projects in Denmark - a new production facility for solid rocket propellant and advanced defense-tech components. Our ambition is significant: we are scaling from the early operational phase to 200+ employees within the next 18 months.

It is a Danish-based defense technology company, part of the international Fire Point Group — a fast-growing ecosystem born out of Ukraine’s innovation and resilience. The group was founded by engineers and entrepreneurs who, during the first months of the full-scale war, decided to use their expertise to create advanced defense technologies — including long-range drones and precision systems.

Joining FPRT now means becoming part of the core team shaping a new high-tech, safety-critical production environment from the ground up.

They are looking for a Maintenance & Engineering Manager who will establish and execute an absolute, zero-compromise reliability strategy from day one.

The Role

As the Maintenance & Engineering Manager, you are responsible for the operational integrity, availability, and safety of all production assets and process equipment. Manufacturing rocket propellant leaves no room for trial and error—our process equipment must be predictable, fully mastered down to the individual component, and maintained at peak condition.

Reporting directly to the Chief Production Officer (CPO), you will lead the technical team in deep equipment mastery, anticipating service intervals with precision, and proactively replacing high-risk components before failures occur. You will work in close functional alignment with Process Engineering, Manufacturing Automation, EHS, Quality, and Production Planning to ensure seamless, compliant operations.

What You Will Do

1. Production Maintenance Strategy & Asset Management

• Develop and implement a preventive and predictive maintenance strategy for all production equipment, focusing on long-cycle and batch-based processes (mixers, thermal curing ovens, polymerization, climate-controlled chambers) to ensure thermal stability and high uptime.

• Minimize downtime by transitioning from reactive repairs to condition-based monitoring and planned interventions.

• Lead the selection, implementation, and management of a CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) to track work orders, asset history, and maintenance costs.

• Integrate maintenance requirements into the equipment acquisition process alongside QA, establishing preventive risk assessments and managing obsolescence planning.

2. Process Utilities & Production Support Engineering

• Oversee point-of-use process utilities directly feeding production lines, such as process vacuum, specialized process gas loops, and line-dedicated thermal fluids.

• Coordinate with internal and external facility teams on utility drop interfaces to ensure production machinery interface readiness.

3. EHS & Process Safety Compliance

• Enforce strict adherence to EHS standards across all equipment maintenance activities.

• Rigorously execute Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures and "Permit to Work" systems on energetic material processing machinery and hazardous equipment zones.

4. Production Spare Parts & Technical Inventory

• Define critical spare parts strategies for production machinery to balance inventory costs with operational risk mitigation.

• Partner with the Warehouse team to track, store, and preserve technical production spares correctly.

• Monitor market lifecycle status for key equipment components and execute end-of-life obsolescence planning.

5. Team Leadership & Technical Development

• Lead, mentor, and schedule a team of production maintenance technicians and equipment specialists.

• Ensure the team is fully trained in safety protocols (ATEX, energetic materials) and advanced technical troubleshooting.

• Plan technician resources and build mechanical redundancy strategies to protect production during interventions or unplanned events.

6. Production Line CapEx & Commissioning Support

• Support the installation, mechanical integration, and commissioning of new production lines with Process Engineering and Automation.

• Provide early input on machine "serviceability and accessibility" during the design phase to eliminate future shop-floor bottlenecks.

First 90 Days – Expected Outcomes

• Critical spare parts inventory analysis completed and gaps identified.

• Preventative Maintenance (PM) schedule established for all key production assets.

• Maintenance team skills matrix assessed and training plan initiated.

• Design of the “obtain equipment” process and equipment lifecycle framework completed in collaboration with QA.

What We Offer

• A rare career opportunity to lead the engineering and maintenance function for one of Denmark's most unique industrial and defense-tech projects.

• A role where your technical expertise directly determines the reliability and safety of high-stakes, safety-critical production.

• A professional, international environment with a clear mission and purpose.

• Brand-new factory & equipment.

• Real authority, Greenfield impact, Zero toxic culture, Mastery over busywork.

• Top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

We Are Looking For

You are a highly structured, disciplined, and hands-on leader who thrives on the shop floor and maintains an absolute zero-compromise approach to equipment safety and operational reliability.

Requirements:

• Education: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Marine Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Experience: 5+ years of maintenance management experience within heavy industry, chemical processing, pharma, defense, or similar high-safety manufacturing environments.

• Leadership: Proven track record of managing technical teams, scheduling resources, and coordinating external contractors and facility service providers.

• Regulatory Knowledge: Experience working in highly regulated environments (ATEX, SEVESO, or similar energetic/hazardous contexts).

• Systems & Methods: Experience implementing or optimizing CMMS systems (e.g., SAP PM, Maximo) and utilizing OEE and Root Cause Analysis (FMEA, 8D, 5 Whys).

• Technical Mastery: Strong working knowledge of mechanical systems (hydraulics, pneumatics, rotating equipment), electrical systems, and industrial automation (PLC, SCADA).

Apply

Due to GDPR rules we are not allowed to receive CV or application through our email system.
